ben_sales: Quick heads-up — ACME cloud asked whether we can run Redwood Private behind Azure ExpressRoute + Private Link for their POC. They want minimal internet egress and strict firewall allowlists. Any red flags?

maria_neteng: That's supported but has a couple of tradeoffs. ExpressRoute can carry traffic to their VNet, Private Link exposes a private endpoint in their VNet that maps to our service. Need to decide: PrivateLink per-customer (good isolation) vs VNet peering + NAT (cheaper at scale).

ben_sales: They care about isolation and compliance, willing to pay extra. Main asks: which ports/hosts to allow, whether BGP is needed, and if we can do certs with their KMS.

alice_se: For POC we usually recommend Private Link + service endpoint. Minimal firewall rules: outbound 443 to our privatelink endpoint IPs and maybe 5000-6000 UDP/TCP for healthchecks? I'll confirm exact ports.

jake_secops: Security questions: 1) Do we support customer-managed keys (CMK) for data at rest in Private? 2) Are audit logs exported to their SIEM? 3) Can we disable public IPs on the Private control plane?

alice_se: Answers: 1) Yes, CMK via KMS/HSM integration for Private deployments. 2) We can stream audit logs to their Event Hub/Log Analytics or S3 equivalent. 3) We can run control plane in private mode (no public IPs) for Private deployment — but requires an egress path for updates if they opt out of air-gapped.

maria_neteng: BGP only needed if they're using ExpressRoute circuit with dynamic routing to advertise on-prem prefixes. For simple Private Link, no BGP required — it's just an ENI/private endpoint in their VNet. If they want cross-prem via TGW/ASN, we should get their ASN and sample routes.

tom_infra: Firewall rules we ask for (POC): allow outbound TLS 443 to privatelink.<region>.redwood-inference.internal (they get IPs when we create endpoint), allow outbound 123/UDP for NTP to our NTP cluster or their internal NTP, and allow connection to our healthcheck range: `10.200.0.0/22`. We'll supply exact CIDRs.

ben_sales: Pricing note from ACME: they expect a delta for PrivateLink + reserved private capacity. Can we get a ballpark for monthly uplift?

alice_se: For small POC (1-2 instances) expect ~$2-5k/mo delta for Private infra + endpoint provisioning. Dedicated capacity / reserved commit changes pricing more — sales will follow up with formal quote.

jake_secops: Also ask about firewall egress for model downloads. If they want to pin models locally, we need to allow our model registry endpoints or provide an offline bundle.

maria_neteng: POC next steps: 1) Customer shares VNet CIDR, transit/TGW design or whether ExpressRoute exists. 2) We provision PrivateLink service -> send IPs. 3) They add firewall rules + test. 4) We validate via connectivity checks and token-auth call.

ben_sales: I'll ping ACME to get VNet details and security questionnaire answers. @alice_se can you prepare the short runbook and the preliminary firewall snippet we can email them?

alice_se: Yep — I'll post a runbook in this thread by EOD with sample iptables/NSG rules and the list of TLS hostnames.

deploy-bot: Deployed private-endpoint template (draft) to staging — ID: pe-template-2024-06-06. Use with caution. :rocket:

tom_infra: When you get their VNet CIDR, also confirm if they use forced tunneling. If so we need to test egress path for OCSP/CRL and our telemetry endpoints.

ben_sales: Great — thanks everyone. I'll update once ACME sends the network config. :thumbsup:
